eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader consensus on the Polymarket heavily favors a highest temperature of 32–33°C in Chongqing on August 9, 2026 (combined ~78.5% implied probability), reflecting current forecast consensus around the long-term August average high of ~32°C.**

This aligns with the market's tight clustering, as the city's subtropical monsoon climate—characterized by high humidity, basin topography that traps heat, and frequent convective rainfall—has produced variable temperatures rather than prolonged extremes this week.

Primary scientific drivers include steering patterns from mid-latitude systems or monsoon influences that limit intense solar heating and promote cloud cover or precipitation, keeping values below the 35–40°C peaks more typical during strong heatwave episodes. Upcoming model updates from the China Meteorological Administration and refined short-range forecasts will be key resolution inputs, with traders weighting these heavily given the day's proximity to the event.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the King Abdulaziz International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 9 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the King Abdulaziz International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/sa/jeddah/OEJN.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Market-implied odds reflect trader focus on whether Jeddah reaches or exceeds typical late-summer peaks amid above-normal regional temperatures.** Forecasts from sources such as AccuWeather and local models indicate daytime maxima near 36–38 °C for August 9, consistent with Jeddah’s coastal Red Sea climate where sea breezes and high humidity often cap extremes below inland values. Seasonal outlooks from Saudi Arabia’s National Center for Meteorology note a 55–80 % chance of above-average warmth through October, supporting the combined 79.5 % probability on 39 °C or higher. Close spreads between the 39 °C and 40 °C+ bins highlight model sensitivity to exact timing of peak heating, wind shifts, and urban heat-island effects that can add 1–2 °C locally. Official station data will resolve the market once the daily maximum is recorded.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent high-pressure ridging across western Europe, part of the latest heatwave episode, is driving subsidence warming, clear skies, and southerly flow that favors afternoon highs near 32°C in Paris on August 10. Ensemble guidance from Météo-France and ECMWF shows limited spread around this value, with urban heat-island effects and low soil moisture from prior hot spells adding a few tenths of a degree. Traders assign over 80% combined probability to 31–33°C outcomes, reflecting model consensus and the narrow window before resolution; lower or higher extremes remain unlikely absent a rapid shift in steering flow or unexpected cloud cover. Updated model runs tomorrow morning represent the key near-term catalyst for any adjustment in implied odds.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent ensemble forecasts from European centers, including ECMWF runs, show Munich's maximum temperature on August 10 likely peaking at 33–34°C under a persistent high-pressure ridge. Subsidence warming in the lower atmosphere, combined with reduced cloud cover and strong solar insolation, drives the expected heat buildup, with 850 hPa temperatures supporting surface values near these levels. Trader consensus assigns nearly equal implied probabilities to 33°C (42.5%) and 34°C (40.5%), reflecting minor model spread in boundary-layer mixing and exact timing of peak heating. Official resolution will rely on DWD station measurements, and the final model consensus update before observation will determine whether conditions tip toward the upper or lower end of this narrow range.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent marine layer and onshore flow are capping coastal heating in Los Angeles, positioning 78–79°F as the market favorite (51.5% implied probability) for the August 10 daily high, followed by 76–77°F (28.5%).**

National Weather Service discussions and recent observations at Los Angeles International Airport (KLAX, the typical resolution station) show a deep marine layer—often 1,400–1,500 feet—producing patchy dense fog, low clouds, and gradual afternoon clearing under moderate southwest winds. This pattern has kept recent daily highs in the mid-70s, well below the August climatological average of ~84–85°F. South African Weather Service guidance and ensemble model consensus point to post-frontal conditions featuring increased cloud cover, light isolated showers along the coast, and northwesterly winds shifting to southeasterly, limiting insolation and keeping maximum temperatures near or slightly below the August climatological average of 17–19 °C. eventMetadata.context_description: The Southwest Monsoon dominating Luzon continues to drive trader sentiment toward a narrow 29–31°C range for Manila’s August 11 high, with 29°C and 30°C each at 22.5% implied probability. Persistent cloud cover and intermittent heavy rains reduce incoming solar radiation and enhance evaporative cooling, keeping daytime maxima near or slightly below the 31°C August climatological average. Active 2026 Pacific typhoon season systems, including recent passages of Dolphin and localized depressions, reinforce this pattern by maintaining moist southwesterly flow and suppressing clear-sky heating episodes that could push readings to 33°C or higher. Updated PAGASA guidance and model consensus on monsoon strength through mid-August remain the key near-term variables that could shift resolution odds.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.
